column5: But we're still friends, right...?\nAnd no matter what, friends stick together.\nSo let's get that blade, and head to Mazeo.
column6: 但我们还是朋友，对吧……？\n不管发生什么，朋友都会并肩同行。\n所以，我们去拿那把剑，然后前往马泽奥。

column5: Oh, I guess I see things differently.\nI have no problem protecting you if things get hairy.\nLet's get that blade, then. We'll take this step-by-step.
column6: 哦，看来我的想法不太一样。\n要是事情变得棘手，我保护你也没问题。\n那就去拿那把剑吧。我们一步一步来。

column5: Well, it's not like we're saving the world or anything.\nI know I make a lot of jokes, but I was being serious!\nI guess we can talk on the way. Let's get that blade.
column6: 好吧，又不是说我们在拯救世界什么的。\n我知道我平时爱开玩笑，但刚才我是认真的！\n我们可以路上再聊。去拿那把剑吧。

column5: Nothing to say? Really?\nOh well, I guess I was hoping for too much.\nLet's get that blade. We'll talk more on the way.
column6: 没什么要说的？真的？\n算了，看来是我期望太高了。\n去拿那把剑吧。路上再多聊。

column5: Yeah, I'm about ready to get off this bridge.\nNot exactly the best place for a heart-to-heart.\nThough honestly, I'm glad you opened up.
column6: 是啊，我差不多该离开这座桥了。\n这里可不是谈心的好地方。\n不过说实话，我很高兴你能敞开心扉。

column5: And actually, I think I've found my purpose.\nI want to fight to protect my closest friends.\nSo about that promise? I'll be here. Right until the end.
column6: 其实，我想我找到了自己的目标。\n我要为守护最亲近的朋友而战。\n所以，那个约定呢？我会一直在这里。直到最后。

column5: I nod, and they smile at one another.{w}\nA few moments later, we continue our trek to The Grand Tree.{w}\nThis time, however, we reach our goal with no interruptions.
column6: 我点点头，她们相视一笑。{w}\n片刻之后，我们继续向巨树跋涉。{w}\n不过这一次，我们一路无阻地抵达了目的地。

column5: As soon as we enter, we all spread out.{w}\nPerhaps covering more ground would help us find it easier.{w}\nHowever, much to our surprise, it's out in the open.
column6: 我们一进去，便四下散开。{w}\n也许搜寻的范围越大，就越容易找到它。{w}\n然而，出乎我们意料，它竟就摆在明处。

column5: Wait, that's it...?
column6: 等等，就是这个……？

column5: It's wrapped up in a sack, in front of The Grand Tree's altar.{w}\nThe general shape and size was easily discernable to me.{w}\nIt was the instrument of my death, and Valinorth's destruction.
column6: 它被裹在一个布袋里，就放在巨树的祭坛前。{w}\n它的大致形状与大小，我一眼便能辨认。{w}\n那是夺走我性命、毁灭瓦利诺斯的凶器。

column5: There's a letter attached to it.\nLet's see what it says.
column6: 上面还附着一封信。\n我们看看写了什么。

column5: Wait, hold on...!\nI don't think we're supposed to touch it.\nWe should probably leave this one to [firstname].
column6: 等等，先别动……！\n我觉得我们不该碰它。\n这件事还是交给[firstname]吧。

column5: Wait, hold on...!\nI don't think we're supposed to touch it.\nWe should probably leave this one to [firstname].
column6: 等等，先别动……！\n我觉得我们不该碰它。\n这件事还是交给[firstname]吧。

column5: I'm sure it's fine as long as it's covered up.\nBut very well, feel free to do the honors.
column6: 只要它还包着，应该就没事。\n不过也好，那就请你来吧。

column5: They both look at me, leaving me little choice in the matter.{w}\nIt's not like they had any choice in this either, however.{w}\nTaking slow steps to the altar, I look down at the letter.
column6: 她们俩都看着我，让我别无选择。{w}\n不过话说回来，她们在这件事上又何尝有过选择。{w}\n我缓步走向祭坛，低头看向那封信。

column5: Well, what does it say?
column6: 那么，上面写了什么？

column5: I kneel down and pull off the letter, breaking some adhesive.{w}\nIt's from Mylus, and it gives us a bit more information.{w}\nNone of us have really left Valinorth, so guidance is helpful.
column6: 我跪下来撕下信纸，扯开了些许黏胶。{w}\n信是迈勒斯写的，给了我们一些补充信息。{w}\n我们谁都没真正离开过瓦利诺斯，所以指点很有帮助。

column5: I put the letter in my pocket, and look at Fortaime and Valessa.{w}\nIt seems that our next objective was clear. Much better than before.{w}\nIf Mylus simply threw us into the wild, we'd get lost immediately.
column6: 我把信揣进口袋，看向福泰姆和瓦莱莎。{w}\n看来我们的下一个目标很明确了。比之前清楚多了。{w}\n要是迈勒斯就这么把我们扔进荒野，我们立马就会迷路。

column5: The Blade of Exodus?\nThat's a bit of a weird name, isn't it?\nDo you think that's the person who made it...?
column6: 流亡之刃？\n这名字有点怪，不是吗？\n你觉得这是打造它的人的名字吗……？

column5: Or maybe it's a title for whoever wields it.\nYou know, something like Seer or Seeress.\nWhat about it...? Should we call you Exodus?
column6: 或者是持有者的称号。\n你知道的，就像先知那样的名号。\n怎么样……？要不我们叫你“流亡”？

column5: Yeah, I agree!\nWe want to blend in, not stand out.\nThat would be like walking around with a huge label.
column6: 对，我同意！\n我们要的是融入人群，而不是引人注目。\n那就像走到哪儿都顶着个大标签一样。

column5: Don't tell me you're considering it...?\nCome on, we need to blend in, not stand out.\nMight as well put a huge label on yourself.
column6: 别告诉我你真在考虑……？\n得了吧，我们需要融入人群，而不是引人注目。\n那还不如直接给自己贴个大标签。

column5: Yeah, especially if The Triumvirate wants it back.\nWalking around as Exodus would put a huge target on us.\nThat's not something we can afford if we want to blend in.
column6: 是啊，尤其三人执政团还想把它夺回去。\n顶着“流亡”的名号到处走，会让我们成为活靶子。\n想融入人群，我们可负担不起这个。

column5: Alright, alright. Forget I suggested it.\nLet's get out of here before we waste too much time.\nWe're supposed to meet someone named Zamira, right?
column6: 好吧好吧，当我没提议过。\n趁还没浪费太多时间，我们赶紧离开这儿。\n我们要去见一个叫扎米拉的人，对吧？

column5: I know them. They typically guard the town gate.\nNo better person to carry out a secret mission in the night.\nI'm glad we'll have a guide. I was starting to worry we'd get lost.
column6: 我认识他们。他们一般是看守城门的人。\n夜里执行秘密任务，没有比他更合适的人选了。\n有向导就好，我正担心我们会迷路呢。

column5: Yeah. None of us have ever left Valinorth before.\nI'm sure it'll be great. We can even check out Sauleberg!\nGrab the blade, [firstname]. The villagers would never question you.
column6: 是啊。我们谁都没离开过瓦利诺斯。\n肯定会很棒的。我们甚至还能去看看索尔伯格！\n拿起那把剑吧，[firstname]。村民们绝不会质疑你的。

column5: Yeah. None of us have ever left Valinorth before.\nI'm sure it'll be great. We can even check out Sauleberg!\nGrab the blade, [firstname]. The villagers would never question you.
column6: 是啊。我们谁都没离开过瓦利诺斯。\n肯定会很棒的。我们甚至还能去看看索尔伯格！\n拿起那把剑吧，[firstname]。村民们绝不会质疑你的。

column5: I nod. As the Seer, they wouldn't care what I carried.{w}\nBut I can understand if they saw an outsider with this blade.{w}\nMylus' plan of using Zamira was definitely the best course of action.
column6: 我点点头。身为先知，他们不会在意我带着什么。{w}\n但我也能理解，若是他们看到外人拿着这把剑会作何感想。{w}\n迈勒斯利用扎米拉的计划，无疑是最佳之策。

column5: I nod. As the Seeress, they wouldn't care what I carried.{w}\nBut I can understand if they saw an outsider with this blade.{w}\nMylus' plan of using Zamira was definitely the best course of action.
column6: 我点点头。身为先知，他们不会在意我带着什么。{w}\n但我也能理解，若是他们看到外人拿着这把剑会作何感想。{w}\n迈勒斯利用扎米拉的计划，无疑是最佳之策。

column5: As we venture to Mazeo, however, some people might stare.{w}\nBut we're in a group, so I doubt they'd try anything.{w}\nI pity the person who picked a fight with the Blade of Exodus.
column6: 不过，当我们前往马泽奥时，或许会有人盯着看。{w}\n但我们结伴而行，我想他们不敢轻举妄动。{w}\n敢跟流亡之刃动手的人，我倒是要同情他了。

column5: I carefully unwrap the package.{w}\nThe sight of the weapon causes me to tense up.{w}\nI can almost feel the pain of last night's vision.
column6: 我小心翼翼地拆开包裹。{w}\n一看到那件武器，我便浑身紧绷。{w}\n昨夜幻象中的痛楚，几乎又涌上心头。

column5: Valessa and Fortaime look down, seeing it for the first time.{w}\nI exchange glances with them, before my eyes return to the blade.{w}\nI grip it for the first time, and that's when everything changes.
column6: 瓦莱莎和福泰姆低下头，第一次见到它。{w}\n我与他们对视一眼，随后目光又落回剑上。{w}\n我第一次握住了它，而就在那一刻，一切都变了。

column5: With a blinding flash of white light, I fall back.{w}\nLanding on the floor, I'm unable to see, or move.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until I can't breathe, either.
column6: 一道刺目的白光闪过，我向后倒去。{w}\n摔在地上，我既看不见，也动弹不得。{w}\n没过多久，我连呼吸都做不到了。

column5: I hear Valessa and Fortaime call out to me.{w}\nBut as my senses are robbed, their shouts slowly fade.{w}\nA series of visions plays out before me, and I can do little but watch.
column6: 我听见瓦莱莎和福泰姆在呼唤我。{w}\n可随着我的感官被剥夺，他们的呼喊也渐渐远去。{w}\n一幕幕幻象在我眼前上演，而我只能眼睁睁看着。

column5: You mean this was all just a trap!?\nNo, I don't believe it. I'm not giving up!
column6: 你是说这一切都只是个陷阱！？\n不，我不信。我绝不放弃！

column5: To think all of that was stored in {i}this{/i}.\nAfter we tell the people, everything will change.
column6: 没想到那么多东西，就封存在{i}这{/i}里面。\n等我们告诉民众之后，一切都会改变。

column5: We will aid you in this fight.\nBut you are no longer a Rebellion.\nToday, you become something {i}much{/i} more.
column6: 我们会在这场战斗中助你一臂之力。\n但你们不再是反抗军了。\n从今天起，你们将成为{i}远为{/i}不凡的存在。

column5: Wait! Think about what you're doing!\nWithout us, there {i}is{/i} no freedom...!
column6: 等等！想想你在做什么！\n没有我们，就{i}根本{/i}没有自由……！

column5: Don't worry. Nothing personal.\nJust playing with the hand I've been dealt.
column6: 别担心。不是针对你。\n只是打好我手里的这副牌罢了。

column5: The shadowed man approaches me, with a dagger in his hand.{w}\nI can't fight back. I can just watch as he sinks it into my gut.{w}\nSoon after, I'm paralyzed on the ground. I can hear him laughing.
column6: 那阴影中的男人手持匕首向我走来。{w}\n我无力反抗，只能眼看他把刀刺进我的腹部。{w}\n紧接着，我瘫倒在地，耳边是他放肆的笑声。

column5: I gasp for air as I grip the spot where he stabbed me.{w}\nValessa and Fortaime let out huge sighs of relief.{w}\nIn my other hand, I hold the Blade of Exodus tightly.
column6: 我喘着粗气，捂住被刺中的地方。{w}\n瓦莱莎和福泰姆长长地松了一口气。{w}\n我的另一只手里，紧紧攥着流亡之刃。

column5: I throw it across the room, as I slowly regain my breath.{w}\nThey help me rise to a sitting position, the concern on their faces clear.{w}\nThankfully, I'm able to relax before they decide to question me.
column6: 我把它扔到房间另一头，慢慢缓过气来。{w}\n他们扶我坐起身，脸上的担忧显而易见。{w}\n幸好，在他们开口追问之前，我先放松了下来。

column5: What happened...?
column6: 发生什么了……？

column5: Wait, how is that possible...?\nThe spirits are the ones who give visions.\nCould it have something to do with your energy?
column6: 等等，这怎么可能……？\n幻象一向是灵体赐予的。\n会不会跟你的灵力有关？

column5: Valessa, it doesn't matter!\nFor now, we just need to make sure he's safe.
column6: 瓦莱莎，那不重要！\n眼下我们只要确保他平安就好。

column5: Valessa, it doesn't matter!\nFor now, we just need to make sure she's safe.
column6: 瓦莱莎，那不重要！\n眼下我们只要确保她平安就好。

column5: Right, sorry.\nWill you be okay? Can you move?
column6: 对，抱歉。\n你还好吗？能活动吗？

column5: Good, I'm glad to hear.\nMylus left a change of clothes for you.\nIt was tucked underneath the blade, see?
column6: 好，听你这么说我就放心了。\n迈勒斯给你留了一套换洗的衣服。\n就塞在剑底下，看到了吗？

column5: She points to the package that held the blade.{w}\nResting there, is a set of battle-ready clothing.{w}\nA holster, or scabbard, is built into the back.
column6: 她指向先前装剑的包裹。{w}\n那里放着一套为战斗准备的衣服。{w}\n背后还缝着一个挂鞘，或者说剑鞘。

column5: Maybe Mylus knew that touching it was risky.\nIf you wear this outfit, you can sheathe the blade.\nIt might be best to conceal it, and minimize contact.
column6: 也许迈勒斯知道碰它是件危险的事。\n穿上这套衣服，你就能把剑收进鞘里。\n最好把它藏起来，尽量减少接触。

column5: Wait, then why didn't he tell us that...?\nSeems like a stupid thing to leave out.
column6: 等等，那他为什么不告诉我们……？\n这么重要的事都不提，也太蠢了。

column5: Hmm. I guess you have a point.\nOh well, I'm glad that things are fine.\nYou should go get changed, [firstname].
column6: 嗯，你说得也有道理。\n算了，没事就好。\n你去换衣服吧，[firstname]。

column5: I guess you have a point.\nOh well, I'm glad that things are fine.\nYou should go get changed, [firstname].
column6: 你说得也有道理。\n算了，没事就好。\n你去换衣服吧，[firstname]。

column5: She tilts her head to an alcove at the back of The Grand Tree.{w}\nI guess it would provide sufficient privacy, so I grab the clothes.{w}\nThey turn their backs to me as an extra gesture of consideration.
column6: 她朝巨树后方的一个壁龛偏了偏头。{w}\n那里应该足够隐蔽，于是我拿起衣服。{w}\n他们转过身去，算是额外的体贴。

column5: It looks like a mixture of Valessa and Fortaime's outfit.{w}\nMade of flexible material, it was clearly ready for a fight.{w}\nThe scabbard is adjustable. I could position it for my dominant hand.
column6: 它看起来像是瓦莱莎和福泰姆服装的结合。{w}\n用料柔韧，一看就是为战斗而备。{w}\n剑鞘可以调节。我可以按惯用手来调整位置。

column5: I tilt it to the left, for easy access with my left hand.{w}\nNot that I expected to be touching the blade all too often.{w}\nWhen the rest of the outfit is on, I walk back out in the open.
column6: 我把它调到左侧，方便左手取用。{w}\n倒也不是说我打算经常碰那把剑。{w}\n穿戴整齐后，我重新走回空地。

column5: I tilt it to the right, for easy access with my right hand.{w}\nNot that I expected to be touching the blade all too often.{w}\nWhen the rest of the outfit is on, I walk back out in the open.
column6: 我把它调到右侧，方便右手取用。{w}\n倒也不是说我打算经常碰那把剑。{w}\n穿戴整齐后，我重新走回空地。

column5: Whoa, that looks really good on you.\nA lot more fitting than that fancy suit.
column6: 哇，你穿这身真好看。\n比那套花哨的西装合身多了。

column5: Whoa, that looks really good on you.\nA lot more fitting than that fancy dress.
column6: 哇，你穿这身真好看。\n比那件花哨的裙子合身多了。

column5: That's everything we need, then?\nI mean, aside from the blade.
column6: 那我们需要的东西都齐了？\n我是说，除了那把剑。

column5: We all look to where I threw it earlier.{w}\nBefore we left, I'd have to touch it again.{w}\nI can sense the anxiety within my friends.
column6: 我们都看向先前我把它扔出去的地方。{w}\n离开之前，我还得再碰它一次。{w}\n我能感觉到朋友们心中的不安。

column5: Look. Whatever happens, we're here for you.\nI doubt it'll be as bad as last time, and you're fine.
column6: 听着。无论发生什么，我们都在你身边。\n我想不会像上次那么糟，而且你现在也没事。

column5: He could've worded that a bit better, but there was truth to it.{w}\nIt was such a shock last time because I didn't expect it at all.{w}\nBut I was the Seer of Valinorth. I was meant to wield this blade.
column6: 他这话说得不太中听，但也不无道理。{w}\n上次之所以那么震惊，是因为我毫无防备。{w}\n但我是瓦利诺斯的先知。这把剑本就该由我来执掌。

column5: He could've worded that a bit better, but there was truth to it.{w}\nIt was such a shock last time because I didn't expect it at all.{w}\nBut I was the Seeress of Valinorth. I was meant to wield this blade.
column6: 他这话说得不太中听，但也不无道理。{w}\n上次之所以那么震惊，是因为我毫无防备。{w}\n但我是瓦利诺斯的先知。这把剑本就该由我来执掌。

column5: I slowly walk towards it, kneeling down when I get there.{w}\nWhatever happened this time, I wouldn't let it control me.{w}\nAs I grab it, I remind myself that I am one with the spirits.
column6: 我缓步走向它，到跟前便跪了下来。{w}\n无论这次会发生什么，我都不会被它左右。{w}\n握住它的那一刻，我提醒自己：我与灵体同在。

column5: The white light overtakes me again, but that's all.{w}\nI can still move, breathe, and sense my surroundings.{w}\nDeep within me, I feel a connection defying explanation.
column6: 白光再次将我笼罩，但也仅此而已。{w}\n我仍能活动、呼吸，感知周围的一切。{w}\n在内心深处，我感到一种无法言说的连结。

column5: It's beautiful, and I'd like to stay this way forever.{w}\nUnfortunately, the feeling soon turns into something more.{w}\nIn a matter of seconds, the source of beauty is one of fright.
column6: 那感觉很美，我愿永远如此。{w}\n可惜，这份感觉很快变成了别的东西。{w}\n不过几秒，美好的源泉便成了恐惧的源头。

column5: I quickly sheathe the blade, to prevent any damage.{w}\nWhatever that was, doing it for too long would hurt me.{w}\nIt seems that using this weapon would require some practice.
column6: 我迅速把剑收入鞘中，以免受伤。{w}\n不管那是什么，持续太久都会伤到我。{w}\n看来要驾驭这件武器，还得下一番功夫。

column5: Well that looked fine to me.\nYou didn't end up on the floor, at least.
column6: 在我看来还挺顺利的。\n至少你没摔在地上。

column5: Now that's what I like to hear!\nGood to know it was just a first time thing.\nHopefully Damek can give us more information.
column6: 这才是我爱听的话！\n幸好只是第一次才会这样。\n但愿达梅克能给我们更多信息。

column5: Whoa, really...?\nMylus was right, then. It takes strength.\nRemind me not to touch that thing anytime soon.
column6: 哇，真的……？\n那迈勒斯说得没错。这需要力量。\n提醒我，最近千万别碰那玩意儿。

column5: I'm curious to learn more about it.\nLike where it came from, and who made it.\nHopefully we figure that out along the way.
column6: 我很好奇想多了解它一些。\n比如它从哪来，又是谁打造的。\n但愿我们能在路上弄明白。

column5: So, should we get going...?\nOr is there anything else we need to do?
column6: 那么，我们该出发了吗……？\n还是说还有什么别的事要办？

column5: We're supposed to meet Zamira on Main Street.\nBut we should save that until we're ready to leave.\nOne last look around Valinorth couldn't hurt.
column6: 我们跟扎米拉约在主街碰头。\n不过还是等我们准备出发时再去吧。\n最后再看一眼瓦利诺斯也无妨。

column5: Yeah, I was thinking about that earlier.\nWouldn't want to leave anything behind.
column6: 是啊，我刚才也在想这事。\n可不想落下什么东西。

column5: A new feature, Party Banter, has been unlocked.{w}\nFollowing this text box, a brief tutorial will display.{w}\nPrevious areas of Valinorth have been updated.
column6: 新功能“队伍闲聊”已解锁。{w}\n本对话框之后，将显示一段简短的教学。{w}\n瓦利诺斯先前的区域已更新。

column5: You can now leave Valinorth via the world map.{w}\nClicking the icon near EXIT, will meet up with Zamira.{w}\nThe icon leading to Main Street will function as normal.
column6: 现在你可以通过世界地图离开瓦利诺斯了。{w}\n点击“出口”附近的图标，就能与扎米拉会合。{w}\n通往主街的图标功能照常。

column5: A faint glow comes from the back of The Grand Tree.{w}\nProbably an indicator of spiritual energy inside.{w}\nBut after what Mylus told us, I wonder how much is left.
column6: 巨树的后方透出微弱的光芒。{w}\n大概是内部灵力的一种征兆。{w}\n但听完迈勒斯的话，我不禁怀疑还剩多少。

column5: Wow, it's so beautiful inside The Grand Tree.\nToo bad they rarely let the scribe-in-training come here.\nI wish I had more time to spend in Valinorth.
column6: 哇，巨树里面真美。\n可惜他们很少让见习书记官来这里。\n真希望我能在瓦利诺斯多待些时日。

column5: Actually, that's not a scribe-in-training rule.\nIt was more like a Fortaime rule, no offense.
column6: 其实，那不是什么见习书记官的规矩。\n更像是针对福泰姆的规矩，无意冒犯。

column5: What's that supposed to mean!?
column6: 你这话是什么意思！？

column5: You're not exactly a quiet person.\nThis is a sacred place, and silence is essential.
column6: 你可不是个安静的人。\n这里是圣地，安静是必须的。

column5: Why didn't you tell me...?\nI would've been quiet, I promise.\nJust like when I go to the library.
column6: 你为什么不告诉我……？\n我保证我会安静的。\n就像我去图书馆时那样。

column5: Hey, I don't make up the rules.\nBut honestly, I wish I would've fought it.\nI didn't realize our time here would be so limited.
column6: 嘿，规矩又不是我定的。\n但说实话，我真希望当初我争过。\n我没意识到我们在这里的时间会这么有限。

column5: I thought we'd be here until we were old and gray.\nBut to think that Valinorth would just be a small phase...?\nYou're not the only one who has regrets, Fortaime.
column6: 我以为我们会在这里待到白发苍苍。\n可瓦利诺斯竟只是人生中短暂的一段……？\n有遗憾的不只你一个，福泰姆。

column5: At least you were allowed inside...!\nI was kept out because of my big mouth?
column6: 至少你还能进去……！\n我就因为嘴大被拦在外面？

column5: Well, I guess I'm the only one to blame...\nI'll try to watch my mouth from now on.
column6: 好吧，看来只能怪我自己……\n从今往后我会尽量管住嘴。

column5: I give you ten minutes, tops.
column6: 我赌你最多撑十分钟。

column5: Hey!
column6: 嘿！

column5: Shane paced around his prison cell, feeling the walls.{w}\nLooking for any structural weaknesses, anything he could use.{w}\nHe'd been in here far too long, and the isolation was messing with him.
column6: 肖恩在牢房里来回踱步，摸索着墙壁。{w}\n寻找任何结构上的薄弱处，任何能利用的东西。{w}\n他被关在这里太久了，与世隔绝让他快疯了。

column5: Come on Shane, there's gotta be something.\nYou were supposed to break out of here ages ago.\nThis mission is a bust. Damek must be worried sick.
column6: 振作点，肖恩，总会有办法的。\n你早就该逃出去了。\n这次任务砸了。达梅克一定担心坏了。

column5: Come on, you {i}need{/i} to do this...!\nNobody else has come through here and lived.\nYou're gonna be the first, Shane, I know it.
column6: 拜托，你{i}必须{/i}做到……！\n还没有别人从这里活着出去过。\n你会是第一个，肖恩，我知道的。

column5: A voice sounds from the doors of the prison.{w}\nSovy enters, laughing at what he just witnessed.
column6: 牢门外传来一个声音。{w}\n索维走了进来，嘲笑着他刚才目睹的一幕。

column5: Looks like you're taking this worse than I thought.\nI need to talk with you Shane, so come close.
column6: 看来你比我想的还要撑不住啊。\n我有话要跟你谈，肖恩，靠近点。

column5: And what makes you think I'll listen?
column6: 你凭什么觉得我会听？

column5: We haven't yet broken out the torture.\nBut trust me, you're walking a fine line.
column6: 我们还没动用酷刑呢。\n但相信我，你正走在刀尖上。

column5: Whatever, just make it quick.\nI hate the sound of your voice.\nThat, and I was enjoying my time alone.
column6: 随便吧，有话快说。\n我讨厌听到你的声音。\n再说，我正享受独处呢。

column5: Tch—!\nYou really don't care whether you live or die...?\nGood. I like that in a potential soldier of mine.
column6: 啧——！\n你还真不在乎自己是死是活……？\n很好。我就喜欢我未来士兵身上的这股劲。

column5: Wait, what...?
column6: 等等，什么……？

column5: Name your weapon proficiencies.
column6: 说说你擅长的武器。

column5: You're the one who caught me, Sovy.\nYou should know full well what weapons I use.
column6: 抓住我的人是你，索维。\n你该很清楚我用什么武器。

column5: I said proficiencies...!\nRemember how easily I took you down?
column6: 我说的是“擅长”……！\n还记得我多轻松就放倒了你吗？

column5: Fine. I'm good with a bow.\nI can play with daggers too, but not as well.\nJust give me some arrows, and point to a target.
column6: 行。我弓箭还行。\n匕首也能耍两下，不过没那么精。\n给我几支箭，再指个靶子就行。

column5: Good, I'll have no problem finding you a bow.\nWe're leaving on a mission, so follow me.\nYou'll be seeing your allies sooner than you thought.
column6: 好，给你找把弓不成问题。\n我们要出任务了，跟我来。\n你会比想象中更早见到你的同伴们。

column5: Wait, are you smiling...?\nShane, I don't think you know what's happening.\nTaking you with me? This is your punishment.
column6: 等等，你在笑……？\n肖恩，我看你还没搞清楚状况。\n带你走？这就是对你的惩罚。

column5: Huh...?
Yes, I'll line up a few of your allies.\nThen you'll show me how well you handle a bow.\nIf you don't obey, I'll make you suffer.
column6: 没错，我会把你的几个同伴排成一排。\n然后你就让我看看你的弓用得多好。\n要是不听话，我就让你吃苦头。

column5: And if you do obey...?\nWell, your friends will think you've defected.\nThey'll give up all hope of rescuing you.
column6: 要是你听话呢……？\n你的朋友就会以为你叛变了。\n他们会彻底放弃救你的念头。

column5: Then I can keep you here as long as I like.\nI know you may not fear death, Shane.\nWhich is why I'll give you something far worse.
column6: 那我就能想关你多久就关你多久。\n我知道你可能不怕死，肖恩。\n所以我要给你一样远比死亡更糟的东西。

column5: Now come with me, there's much to discuss.\nAnd remember what will happen if you disobey.\nIt's time to realize that you belong to {i}me{/i}.
column6: 现在跟我来，有很多事要谈。\n记住不听话会有什么下场。\n是时候认清，你属于{i}我{/i}了。

column5: Look, you can see some of the roots...!\nThey say The Grand Tree reaches all over Alestia.\nIn that way, Valinorth is connected to everything.
column6: 看，能看到一些树根……！\n据说巨树的根系遍及整个阿莱斯提亚。\n这样说来，瓦利诺斯与万物都相连。

column5: Mark my words, [firstname].\nOne day I'm going to climb The Grand Tree.\nIt's my calling, I can feel it...!
column6: 记住我的话，[firstname]。\n总有一天我要爬上巨树。\n这是我的使命，我能感觉到……！

column5: Mark my words, [firstname].\nOne day I'm going to climb The Grand Tree.\nIt's my calling, I can feel it...!
column6: 记住我的话，[firstname]。\n总有一天我要爬上巨树。\n这是我的使命，我能感觉到……！

column5: We enter Mylus' House with an aura of purpose.{w}\nThough they didn't know what I saw, they knew it was important.{w}\nWe see him shuffling papers at his table, oblivious to our existence.
column6: 我们带着一股郑重其事的气息走进迈勒斯家。{w}\n尽管他们不知道我看到了什么，却知道那很重要。{w}\n他正在桌边翻弄纸张，丝毫没注意到我们。

column5: Hey, Mylus...\nWe need to have a word.
column6: 嘿，迈勒斯……\n我们得跟你谈谈。

column5: He doesn't seem to respond, and continues his business.{w}\nFortaime seems anxious, and taps his foot on the floor.{w}\nA few moments later, Valessa gives up and interjects.
column6: 他似乎没有回应，继续忙自己的事。{w}\n福泰姆显得焦躁，脚尖不停点地。{w}\n片刻之后，瓦莱莎放弃等待，插了话。

column5: Mylus, snap out of it!\nWe need to talk about something important!
column6: 迈勒斯，清醒一点！\n我们有重要的事要谈！

column5: She slams a fist down on the table, startling Mylus.{w}\nHe jumps back a few feet in fright, and then laughs.{w}\nWhatever he was looking at, it fully engrossed him.
column6: 她一拳头砸在桌上，惊得迈勒斯一跳。{w}\n他吓得后退了几步，随即笑了起来。{w}\n不管他刚才在看什么，都让他全神贯注。

column5: You know what they say about death, right...?\nWhen we die, we go on to live in the realm of spirits.\nWith that logic, spiritual energy should be infinite.
column6: 你知道关于死亡的传说吧……？\n我们死后，灵会在灵界继续存续。\n按这个逻辑，灵力本应无穷无尽。

column5: I'm not really sure how to respond to that...?\nI mean, we've had Seers and Scribes for thousands of years.\nI'm pretty sure we'll have them for thousands more to come.
column6: 我真不知道该怎么回应你……？\n我是说，先知和书记官已经存在了几千年。\n我相信往后几千年的光景也不例外。

column5: Wouldn't that be beautiful...?\nSorry for rambling, but we should all have a seat.\nI'm afraid things aren't going to go as planned.
column6: 那该多好啊……？\n抱歉我扯远了，不过我们都坐下来吧。\n恐怕事情不会按计划发展了。

column5: He motions to the back of his house, a carpeted area.{w}\nWith no chairs in sight, it looks like we'd be sitting on the floor.{w}\nWe make our way over there, questioning just what he meant.
column6: 他示意我们到他家后方铺着地毯的一角。{w}\n那里看不到椅子，看来我们得坐在地上。{w}\n我们走过去，心里琢磨着他那话到底是什么意思。

column5: I think we were going to say the same thing to you.\nI mean, [firstname] had a vision last night. A big one.\nHopefully we have enough time to get through all of this.
column6: 其实我们正打算跟你说同样的话。\n我是说，[firstname]昨晚看到了幻象。很重要的那种。\n但愿我们有足够的时间把这些都说完。

column5: I think we were going to say the same thing to you.\nI mean, [firstname] had a vision last night. A big one.\nHopefully we have enough time to get through all of this.
column6: 其实我们正打算跟你说同样的话。\n我是说，[firstname]昨晚看到了幻象。很重要的那种。\n但愿我们有足够的时间把这些都说完。

column5: Well, unfortunately, I'm past the point of subtlety.\nSo in the interest of time, I'll get right to it.\nThe induction ceremony is henceforth cancelled.
column6: 唉，可惜我已经没心思绕弯子了。\n为了省时间，我就直说了。\n授任仪式即日起取消。

column5: What!? You can't be serious!\nYou hype us all up, and take it away?\nThere better be an explanation for this!
column6: 什么！？你不是认真的吧！\n你把我们的兴致都提起来了，然后说取消就取消？\n最好给个解释！

column5: Fortaime is fuming with anger, and very upset.{w}\nI guess Mylus was right, plans have changed.{w}\nBut the timing, along with my vision, was odd.
column6: 福泰姆气得冒烟，满心愤懑。{w}\n看来迈勒斯说得没错，计划有变。{w}\n但这时机，再加上我的幻象，实在蹊跷。

column5: What's going on here, Mylus...?
column6: 到底怎么回事，迈勒斯……？

column5: I'm afraid that's a very complicated answer.\nLet's back things up a few moments.\n[firstname]. Tell us about the vision you had.
column6: 恐怕这个答案很复杂。\n我们先倒回一会儿。\n[firstname]。说说你看到的幻象吧。

column5: I'm afraid that's a very complicated answer.\nLet's back things up a few moments.\n[firstname]. Tell us about the vision you had.
column6: 恐怕这个答案很复杂。\n我们先倒回一会儿。\n[firstname]。说说你看到的幻象吧。

column5: I take a deep breath, as we all sit down.{w}\nThat was the moment I told them everything.{w}\nHow Valinorth was destroyed by The Triumvirate.
column6: 我们都坐下时，我深吸了一口气。{w}\n就在那一刻，我把一切都告诉了他们。{w}\n瓦利诺斯是如何被三人执政团毁灭的。

column5: I told them about the blaze, and the agony.{w}\nHow the man who led the attack had a mystical blade.{w}\nNot only did it kill Ulric, but it killed me as well.
column6: 我向他们讲述了那场大火，那份痛苦。{w}\n讲述了领头之人手持一把神秘之剑。{w}\n它不仅杀了乌尔里克，也杀了我。

column5: When I finish my story, I'm met with silence.{w}\nThey look amongst themselves, in shock and confusion.{w}\nThat's fine. It was a lot to process all at once.
column6: 我讲完后，迎接我的是一片沉默。{w}\n他们面面相觑，震惊又困惑。{w}\n没关系。一下子要消化的东西太多了。

column5: Just as I expected.\nIt was only a matter of time before you saw it.\nThat is, if the spirits truly cared about our protection.
column6: 正如我所料。\n你看到它只是早晚的事。\n前提是，灵体真的在意庇护我们。

column5: Wait, slow down a minute...!\nHow do we know nothing was lost in translation?\nRemember how abstract visions are known to be?
column6: 等等，慢一点……！\n我们怎么知道转述中没有遗漏？\n还记得幻象一向有多抽象吗？

column5: I can confirm that an attack is imminent.\nBesides, Valessa, you know visions aren't like that.\nThe spirits have gotten strong enough, that's no longer an issue.
column6: 我可以确认，袭击迫在眉睫。\n再说，瓦莱莎，你也知道幻象不是那样的。\n灵体已经足够强大，这不再是问题了。

column5: But this can't be true...
column6: 但这不可能是真的……

column5: It is, and unfortunately it's just the start.\nBut there are still some important matters at hand.\nBefore I send you off, I'll tell you everything.
column6: 是真的，而且可惜这只是个开始。\n但眼下还有几件要紧的事。\n在送你们出发之前，我会把一切都告诉你们。

column5: He smiles at each of us before taking a deep breath.{w}\nI notice large bags under his eyes, signs of unrest.{w}\nHe must've been living with this secret for a while.
column6: 他冲我们每个人笑了笑，然后深吸一口气。{w}\n我注意到他眼下浓重的黑眼圈，是寝食难安的痕迹。{w}\n他一定独自守着这个秘密很久了。

column5: I didn't want to tell you until you needed to know.\nI'm just lucky that this vision waited until I was ready.\nThe Triumvirate wants to occupy Valinorth, as they did Mazeo.
column6: 在你们需要知道之前，我本不想说。\n幸好这个幻象一直等到我准备妥当才出现。\n三人执政团想占领瓦利诺斯，就像他们对待马泽奥那样。

column5: I know what you three lost in Mazeo, and I'm sorry.\nBut what they plan to bring to Valinorth is far, far worse.\nPunishment for my Father's involvement with The Rebellion.
column6: 我知道你们三个在马泽奥失去了什么，我很抱歉。\n但他们打算带给瓦利诺斯的，要糟糕得多。\n那是对我父亲参与反抗军的惩罚。

column5: Just like that empty armor seemed to imply.{w}\nSo Valinorth {i}did{/i} have some relation to The Rebellion.{w}\nAnd it wasn't just during Mylus' short reign, either.
column6: 正如那副空铠甲似乎暗示的那样。{w}\n所以瓦利诺斯{i}确实{/i}与反抗军有些关联。{w}\n而且还不只是在迈勒斯短暂的执政期间。

column5: We're supposed to be non-partisan...
column6: 我们本该保持中立的……

column5: Yeah, that's our whole deal...!\nWhy would your Father do that to us?
column6: 是啊，那是我们的立身之本……！\n你父亲为什么要那样对我们？

column5: I'll never forgive you, Mylus!\nYour Father is responsible for all of this...?\nHe betrayed Valinorth the moment he helped them!
column6: 我永远不会原谅你，迈勒斯！\n这一切都要怪你父亲……？\n他出手相助的那一刻，就背叛了瓦利诺斯！

column5: Understandable, but this is not my fault.\nSurely you know about my Father's disappearance.\nBut have you heard the stories of the recent Rebel victory?
column6: 可以理解，但这不是我的错。\n你肯定知道我父亲失踪的事。\n可你听说过最近反抗军胜利的传闻吗？

column5: Rebel victory?
column6: 反抗军胜利？

column5: The blade that [firstname] mentioned.\nIt was taken from The Triumvirate.\nWithout it, they are weak and vulnerable.
column6: 就是[firstname]提到的那把剑。\n它从三人执政团手中被夺走了。\n没有它，他们就虚弱而脆弱。

column5: The blade that [firstname] mentioned.\nIt was taken from The Triumvirate.\nWithout it, they are weak and vulnerable.
column6: 就是[firstname]提到的那把剑。\n它从三人执政团手中被夺走了。\n没有它，他们就虚弱而脆弱。

column5: But it was not an easy feat to accomplish.\nIn their pursuit of the blade, many people died.\nIncluding the leader of The Rebellion itself.
column6: 但这绝非易事。\n为了夺取那把剑，许多人丧命。\n包括反抗军领袖本人。

column5: The new leader, Damek, sent it here for safekeeping.\nI hid it in The Grand Tree, where no one would find it.\nI want you to take it, and seek out Damek in Mazeo.
column6: 新任领袖达梅克把它送到这里妥善保管。\n我把它藏在巨树里，那里没人找得到。\n我要你们取走它，然后去马泽奥找达梅克。

column5: Hey, slow down!\nThis makes sense to you, but it's all a blur to us.\nYour Father was one of the men that died to get this blade?
column6: 嘿，慢着！\n这些你听着明白，我们却一头雾水。\n你父亲就是为夺取这把剑而死的人之一？

column5: Indeed he was, Fortaime.\nThe Rebel Leader's death. My Father's disappearance.\nI'm afraid those are intricately connected.
column6: 正是如此，福泰姆。\n反抗军领袖之死。我父亲的失踪。\n恐怕这两件事有着盘根错节的联系。

column5: You mean...?
column6: 你是说……？

column5: Yes, I do.\nMy Father didn't work with The Rebellion. He created it.\nThe first allegiance in Valinorth's entire history.
column6: 没错。\n我父亲并不是与反抗军合作。是他创建了它。\n这是瓦利诺斯有史以来的第一次结盟。

column5: Whoa...
He formed an allegiance with insurgents in Mazeo.\nTogether they grew, and created a large army.\nLarge enough to steal The Triumvirate's sacred blade.
column6: 他与马泽奥的起义者结成了同盟。\n他们一同壮大，组建了一支庞大的军队。\n大到足以从三人执政团手中盗走那把圣剑。

column5: I don't understand why he'd do that!\nWe're fine on our own, we always have been.
column6: 我不明白他为什么要那样做！\n我们独自就过得很好，一直都是。

column5: Times are changing, and leaving us behind.\nI'm afraid that Valinorth is a dying culture, Valessa.\nWhat I am about to tell you, must not leave this room.
column6: 时代在变，正把我们抛在身后。\n恐怕瓦利诺斯是个正在消亡的文明，瓦莱莎。\n我接下来要说的，绝不能传出这个房间。

column5: What is it...?
column6: 是什么……？

column5: You know of Sauleberg, right?\nHow it houses the spirit idol of Valinorth?
column6: 你知道索尔伯格吧？\n知道那里供奉着瓦利诺斯的灵像？

column5: Yes, of course.\nBut it's been blocked off for a long time.\nI've never gotten to see a spirit idol in person.
column6: 当然知道。\n但那里已经被封锁很久了。\n我还从没亲眼见过灵像。

column5: I'm afraid it might remain that way.\n[firstname]. On the eve of your birth, it went dark.\nValinorth is living on limited spiritual energy.
column6: 恐怕它会一直如此。\n[firstname]。就在你出生前夜，它熄灭了。\n瓦利诺斯如今靠着有限的灵力维生。

column5: I'm afraid it might remain that way.\n[firstname]. On the eve of your birth, it went dark.\nValinorth is living on limited spiritual energy.
column6: 恐怕它会一直如此。\n[firstname]。就在你出生前夜，它熄灭了。\n瓦利诺斯如今靠着有限的灵力维生。

column5: There's no way I believe that, Mylus.\nOur connection with the spirits is eternal.
column6: 我绝不相信，迈勒斯。\n我们与灵体的连结是永恒的。

column5: I wish that were the case, Fortaime.\nIt pains me to say this, but it's true.\n[firstname]. You are the last Seer we shall ever have.
column6: 我也希望如此，福泰姆。\n这话说出来让我心痛，但它是真的。\n[firstname]。你是我们最后一个先知了。

column5: I wish that were the case, Fortaime.\nIt pains me to say this, but it's true.\n[firstname]. You are the last Seeress we shall ever have.
column6: 我也希望如此，福泰姆。\n这话说出来让我心痛，但它是真的。\n[firstname]。你是我们最后一个先知了。

column5: Normally, the spirit idol chooses a child.\nThat child is imparted with a surge of spiritual energy.\nWhen they pass away, it does the same to the next generation.
column6: 通常，灵像会挑选一个孩子。\n将一股灵力注入那孩子体内。\n待他们离世，又会同样传给下一代。

column5: But you, [firstname]. It gave {i}everything{/i} to you.\nLike the spirit realm is making one final push.\nI don't know why, but I have my theories.
column6: 但你，[firstname]。它把{i}一切{/i}都给了你。\n仿佛灵界在做最后的奋力一搏。\n我不知道为什么，但我有自己的猜想。

column5: But you, [firstname]. It gave {i}everything{/i} to you.\nLike the spirit realm is making one final push.\nI don't know why, but I have my theories.
column6: 但你，[firstname]。它把{i}一切{/i}都给了你。\n仿佛灵界在做最后的奋力一搏。\n我不知道为什么，但我有自己的猜想。

column5: It sounds like the spirits have given up on us.\nPerhaps we took their gift for granted, and abused them.\nWithout that idol, and their energy, what will happen to us?
column6: 听起来像是灵体已经放弃我们了。\n也许我们把他们的恩赐视为理所当然，还滥用了他们。\n没有了那尊灵像，没有了他们的灵力，我们会怎样？

column5: I expect that Valinorth will become like any other nation.\nWe'll take history into our own hands, rather than act on guidance.\nIt's not a bad thing, and I don't think the spirits \"gave up\" on us.
column6: 我预计瓦利诺斯会变得和其他任何国家一样。\n我们将自己掌握历史，而非听凭指引行事。\n这不是坏事，我也不认为灵体“放弃”了我们。

column5: In fact, I think it's the opposite.\nThey're placing all of their hope on us.\n[firstname], and that blade, can save us all.
column6: 事实上，我觉得恰恰相反。\n他们把全部希望都寄托在我们身上。\n[firstname]，还有那把剑，能拯救我们所有人。

column5: In fact, I think it's the opposite.\nThey're placing all of their hope on us.\n[firstname], and that blade, can save us all.
column6: 事实上，我觉得恰恰相反。\n他们把全部希望都寄托在我们身上。\n[firstname]，还有那把剑，能拯救我们所有人。

column5: Back to that blade again...?\nWhat does that have to do with all of this?
column6: 又回到那把剑了……？\n它跟这一切有什么关系？

column5: It's not an ordinary blade, as you've been told.\nIn order to harness it, you need remarkable strength.\nOr, in other words, a vast amount of spiritual energy.
column6: 正如你所听说的，它不是一把普通的剑。\n要驾驭它，你需要非凡的力量。\n换言之，是庞大的灵力。

column5: [firstname], I think the spirits chose you to wield this blade.\nTo take it, join The Rebels in Mazeo, and defeat The Triumvirate.\nI know this is asking a lot of you, but we always follow their lead.
column6: [firstname]，我认为是灵体选中了你来执掌这把剑。\n取走它，去马泽奥加入反抗军，击败三人执政团。\n我知道这对你要求很高，但我们一向遵从他们的指引。

column5: [firstname], I think the spirits chose you to wield this blade.\nTo take it, join The Rebels in Mazeo, and defeat The Triumvirate.\nI know this is asking a lot of you, but we always follow their lead.
column6: [firstname]，我认为是灵体选中了你来执掌这把剑。\n取走它，去马泽奥加入反抗军，击败三人执政团。\n我知道这对你要求很高，但我们一向遵从他们的指引。

column5: Valinorth may be attacked, but we can rebuild from the ashes.\nOur true goal here should be the destruction of The Triumvirate.\nHistory should be in our hands, not in the hands of unjust Gods.
column6: 瓦利诺斯也许会受到袭击，但我们能从灰烬中重建。\n我们真正的目标，应当是摧毁三人执政团。\n历史该掌握在我们手中，而非不义之神的手中。

column5: So that's why your Father formed this alliance?\nTo take control of our history in the spirits' absence?\nAnd to make sure The Triumvirate doesn't dictate our future?
column6: 所以这就是你父亲结成同盟的原因？\n在灵体缺席之际，掌控我们的历史？\n并确保三人执政团无法主宰我们的未来？

column5: He wanted to strengthen our bonds with outsiders as well.\nWithout visions, we have to take things as they come.\nForesight helped us out, but we won't always have it.
column6: 他也想加深我们与外界的关系。\n没有幻象，我们只能走一步看一步。\n预知曾助我们一臂之力，但我们不会永远拥有它。

column5: What we do have, however, is the potential of [firstname].\nI think that's why he sacrificed himself to get this blade.\nHe knew that you'd be able to wield it, and achieve liberation.
column6: 然而，我们拥有的是[firstname]的潜力。\n我想这就是他牺牲自己去夺取这把剑的原因。\n他知道你能够执掌它，并实现解放。

column5: What we do have, however, is the potential of [firstname].\nI think that's why he sacrificed himself to get this blade.\nHe knew that you'd be able to wield it, and achieve liberation.
column6: 然而，我们拥有的是[firstname]的潜力。\n我想这就是他牺牲自己去夺取这把剑的原因。\n他知道你能够执掌它，并实现解放。

column5: Please, take the blade, and flee to Mazeo.\nWhen the ceremony is supposed to start, I'll tell the people.\nThey're all rounding up, so it'll be easy to evacuate.
column6: 请带上这把剑，逃去马泽奥。\n等仪式该开始的时候，我会告诉民众。\n他们都会聚集起来，疏散起来也方便。

column5: We might be a bit behind, but we'll meet in Mazeo.\nThere's lots to plan, and little time to plan it.\nWe'll need new homes, and blades for any volunteers.
column6: 我们或许会落后一些，但会在马泽奥会合。\n要筹划的事很多，时间却很少。\n我们需要新家园，还要为志愿者备好兵器。

column5: As far as I can tell, this is not up for debate.\nIf you think it is, then consider it an order from your Elder.\nLeave as soon as you're able, and we'll meet again soon.
column6: 依我看，这事没得商量。\n你要是不服，就当成长老给你的命令。\n尽快动身，我们很快会再见的。

column5: He stands up, and walks away.{w}\nMoments later, he's back to his usual business.{w}\nWe exchange glances with one another, overwhelmed.
column6: 他站起身，走开了。{w}\n片刻之后，他又回到了平日的事务中。{w}\n我们面面相觑，不知所措。

column5: Listen, I'm gonna try and be the voice of reason here.\nMylus said a lot of stuff, and it could be true or false.\nBut if an attack is coming? We should go either way.
column6: 听着，我想在这里当一回理性之声。\n迈勒斯说了很多，真假难辨。\n但要是真有袭击要来？无论如何我们都该走。

column5: Especially if there's a weapon we can use?\nI think we should grab it from The Grand Tree first.\nAgain, not siding with anyone here, just using logic.
column6: 尤其还有一件我们能用的武器？\n我觉得我们应该先去巨树把它取来。\n再说一遍，我不是站谁的边，只是讲道理。

column5: Yeah, you're right.\nWe'd do the same thing even if Mylus didn't tell us to.\nFind something to defend ourselves with, and leave Valinorth.
column6: 是啊，你说得对。\n就算迈勒斯不说，我们也会这么做。\n找点东西防身，然后离开瓦利诺斯。

column5: But he said the spirits gave you all their power?\nAnd they cut their influence from Valinorth for good?\nThis changes Alestia's entire history, not just our actions.
column6: 但他说灵体把全部力量都给了你？\n还永久切断了他们在瓦利诺斯的影响？\n这改变的是整个阿莱斯提亚的历史，而不只是我们的行动。

column5: I can't say I fully understand, but it makes sense.\nMylus' Father foresaw all of this, and took action.\nI feel hatred. But at the same time, I feel hope.
column6: 我不能说我完全明白，但这也说得通。\n迈勒斯的父亲预见了这一切，并采取了行动。\n我心中有恨。但与此同时，也怀有希望。

column5: Let's take this one step at a time, Valessa.\nWe'll grab the weapon, and make our way out of here.\nThe rest can fall into place as we move on.
column6: 我们一步一步来吧，瓦莱莎。\n先拿到武器，再想办法离开这里。\n其余的，边走边看自然会有头绪。

column5: So, to The Grand Tree, then?\nI'll try to maintain one modicum of sanity.\nIt's not like our lives were just turned around.
column6: 那么，去巨树？\n我会尽量保持一丝理智。\n又不是说我们的生活刚刚天翻地覆了。

column5: I'm sure we'll manage, as long as we're together...\nI'm not giving up on any of you, I promise.
column6: 只要我们在一起，我相信总能应付……\n我向你们保证，我不会放弃你们任何一个人。

column5: There's nothing we can't do if we all pitch in.\nLet's go to The Grand Tree, and get that blade!
column6: 只要大家齐心协力，就没有办不到的事。\n走，去巨树，把那把剑拿到手！

column5: Hmm...
Hey, it's a ladder!
column6: 嘿，是架梯子！

column5: Hmm...
Hmm...
I wonder what Valinorth's future truly holds.
column6: 不知道瓦利诺斯的未来究竟会如何。

column5: I had no idea that they were hiding such a secret.\nValinorth could run out of spiritual energy for good...?\nThe cold from Eastcrown could easily kill us off!
column6: 我完全不知道他们还藏着这样的秘密。\n瓦利诺斯的灵力可能会彻底枯竭……？\n东冠的寒气轻易就能要了我们的命！

column5: Fortaime, don't worry.\nIt could be thousands of years before we run out.\nBesides, at this point, it's still conjecture.
column6: 福泰姆，别担心。\n也许还要几千年才会耗尽。\n再说，眼下这还只是猜测。

column5: It's a mess underneath the desk as well.{w}\nI guess Mylus has more pressing matters on his mind.{w}\nIt must've been relieving to tell us all that he did.
column6: 桌子底下也乱成一团。{w}\n看来迈勒斯心里有更要紧的事。{w}\n把那些都告诉我们，他一定松了口气。

column5: I've never been able to see the Bloodleaves fall.{w}\nMaybe one day, as I've heard it's quite the sight.
column6: 我从没见过血叶飘落。{w}\n也许有一天吧，听说那景象相当壮观。

column5: I examine the table, looking at the scattered pieces of paper.{w}\nMylus is deep in his studies, and I'd really hate to bother him.{w}\nI want to read some as well, so I try to grab something he's put aside.
column6: 我端详着桌子，看着散落的纸张。{w}\n迈勒斯正埋头钻研，我实在不想打扰他。{w}\n我也想读一些，于是试着去拿他搁在一旁的东西。

column5: Eastcrown is a pretty scary place.\nI've thought about going there, but I'm too scared.\nApparently, it's cold enough to kill you in minutes!
column6: 东冠是个相当可怕的地方。\n我想过去那儿，但胆子不够。\n据说那里冷得几分钟就能要命！

column5: \"The Fall of the Bloodleaves\" is beautiful though.\nI've seen it a couple times since I was born.\nNot sure what other purpose Eastcrown serves.
column6: 不过“血叶飘落”确实很美。\n我出生以来见过几次。\n不知道东冠还有别的什么用处。

column5: I wonder what Valinorth's future truly holds.
column6: 不知道瓦利诺斯的未来究竟会如何。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: It's a little overwhelming, to be honest.\nI know I acted all cool, but I'm not really sure.\nI'm used to a simple life, and now that's all gone.
column6: 说实话，有点让人招架不住。\n我知道我装作很淡定，其实心里没底。\n我习惯了简单的生活，如今一切都没了。

column5: As far as I know, Valinorth is the last spiritual nation.\nIf we lose our connection, what's going to happen?\nWill Alestia just be completely devoid of spirits?
column6: 据我所知，瓦利诺斯是最后一个灵性国度。\n要是我们失去了连结，会怎么样？\n阿莱斯提亚会彻底没有灵体吗？

column5: And not only that, but The Triumvirate being evil?\nAs far as I know, they've always been benevolent.\nI know what we lost in Mazeo, but I've moved on.
column6: 不止如此，三人执政团是邪恶的？\n据我所知，他们一向仁慈。\n我知道我们在马泽奥失去了什么，但我已经释怀了。

column5: Anyway, I can process all of that later.\nI'm more worried about what's going to happen to {i}us{/i}.\nNot Valinorth, or Alestia. Just you, me, and Valessa.
column6: 总之，那些我可以以后再慢慢消化。\n我更担心{i}我们{/i}会怎样。\n不是瓦利诺斯，也不是阿莱斯提亚。只是你、我，还有瓦莱莎。

column5: Nothing anymore, I'm afraid.\nIt seems their goals have changed to conquest.\nWith Mazeo, it made sense. But not with us.
column6: 恐怕已经没有信任可言了。\n看来他们的目标已经变成了征服。\n对马泽奥，还说得通。但对我们，说不通。

column5: I thought they were our Gods. Our protectors.\nI'm starting to doubt that they even cared.\nI mean, was this their goal all along?
column6: 我以为他们是我们的神明。我们的庇护者。\n我开始怀疑他们是否真的在意过。\n我是说，这难道一直是他们的目的？

column5: All four nations, under their thumb.\nIf they just asked first, we could've cut a deal.\nBut straight to violence? I don't get it.
column6: 四个国家，全都任他们摆布。\n要是他们先开口商量，我们本可以达成协议。\n可一上来就用暴力？我真不明白。

column5: Yeah, and part of me wishes we still could.\nI mean, the attack hasn't happened yet.\nBut I know that's a stupid wish to have.
column6: 是啊，我有一部分还盼着能有那个机会。\n毕竟，袭击还没发生。\n但我知道这是个愚蠢的念头。

column5: You don't beg for your life against those odds.\nThey're coming with everything they've got.\nAnd from what you said, their power is incredible.
column6: 面对那样的实力悬殊，求饶也没用。\n他们会倾巢而出。\n而且照你说的，他们的力量强得可怕。

column5: Yeah, there's no sense begging for lenience.\nNormally, I'd say that it's impossible to win.\nBut with that blade? Things seem different to me.
column6: 是啊，求他们手下留情毫无意义。\n换作平时，我会说这场仗根本赢不了。\n但有了那把剑？在我看来就不一样了。

column5: Mylus said it was important to them, right?\nIf they're weak, we can't hold back.\nThis is our chance to save Alestia!
column6: 迈勒斯说那对他们很重要，对吧？\n既然他们虚弱，我们就不能留手。\n这是我们拯救阿莱斯提亚的机会！

column5: Yeah, but not as good as us.\nAlestia would be better if the spirits were everywhere.\nValinorth is perfect, and we were truly lucky to live here.
column6: 是啊，但没我们这么好。\n要是灵体无处不在，阿莱斯提亚会更好。\n瓦利诺斯是完美的，能住在这里，我们真的很幸运。

column5: But I guess those days are coming to an end.\nWithout spiritual energy, we'll succumb to the cold.\nThe winds from Eastcrown will take over Valinorth.
column6: 但我想那样的日子要结束了。\n没有灵力，我们会败给严寒。\n东冠吹来的寒风将吞噬瓦利诺斯。

column5: I hope there's something we can do.\nMaybe after this, we should come back home.\nIf we could just get that idol to shine again.
column6: 希望能有办法。\n也许这件事之后，我们该回家看看。\n要是能让那尊灵像再次亮起来就好了。

column5: Thanks, that means a lot to me.\nBut I wouldn't want to come off as whiny.\nRight now, we need to combine our strengths.
column6: 谢谢，这对我意义重大。\n但我不想显得像是在抱怨。\n眼下，我们需要齐心协力。

column5: A pity party seems appealing, but it'd be a waste.\nWe can't afford to throw away the sacrifice of Mylus' Father.
column6: 自怨自艾虽然诱人，却只是浪费时间。\n我们不能辜负迈勒斯父亲的牺牲。

column5: Yeah, definitely!\nWe're a team for a reason.\nThere's nothing we can't handle!
column6: 是啊，当然！\n我们是一支队伍，这不是没有理由的。\n没有什么我们应付不了！

column5: I'm ready whenever you are, [firstname].\nLet's grab that blade and head to Mazeo.\nWhatever you need, I'll be by your side.
column6: 你准备好了我随时出发，[firstname]。\n去拿那把剑，然后前往马泽奥。\n无论你需要什么，我都会在你身边。

column5: I never thought I'd be leaving Valinorth, [firstname].\nIn fact, I came to terms with that a long time ago.\nBut here I am, leaving it behind for good, and I'm scared.
column6: 我从没想过自己会离开瓦利诺斯，[firstname]。\n其实，我早就认命了。\n可如今我真的要永远离开它了，我很害怕。

column5: Everything I've read about the outside world is scary.\nPiracy, deathly cold, and even deathly heat.\nWe had it good here. A really nice middle ground.
column6: 我读过的关于外面世界的一切都很可怕。\n海盗、致命的严寒，甚至还有致命酷热。\n我们这里日子过得好。一个很舒适的中庸之地。

column5: This is where it gets confusing for me, though.\nMazeo was supposed to be safer because of The Triumvirate.\nThey occupied it, with force, but they've kept it peaceful.
column6: 不过，让我困惑的地方在这里。\n因为有三人执政团，马泽奥本该更安全。\n他们用武力占领了那里，却也维持了和平。

column5: They could easily do the same thing to Valinorth.\nBut killing everyone, and burning it to the ground?\nThey've crossed a line that no one ever should.
column6: 他们完全可以把同样的手段用在瓦利诺斯。\n但杀光所有人，再一把火烧成灰烬？\n他们越过了任何人都不该越过的底线。

column5: I'm sure it might be worse in my head.\nBut with all the stuff I've read, it's still scary.\nI'm used to routine, so anything new is frightening.
column6: 我脑子里想的也许比现实更糟。\n但读了那么多东西，还是觉得吓人。\n我习惯了按部就班，所以任何新鲜事都让我害怕。

column5: Mazeo is full of merchants, pirates, and mercenaries.\nLet's do our best not to make anyone mad.\nYou never know how far their influence spreads.
column6: 马泽奥到处都是商人、海盗和雇佣兵。\n我们尽量别惹恼任何人。\n你永远不知道他们的势力能伸多远。

column5: Whoa, really?\nYou think we could take on pirates?\nThat's a bit far-fetched, if you ask me.
column6: 哇，真的？\n你觉得我们能对付海盗？\n要我说，这有点异想天开。

column5: But I guess we make a pretty good team.\nIf things get bad, we can play the status card.\nDon't want Mazeo-Valinorth relations to suffer.
column6: 不过我想我们配合得还不错。\n要是事情闹大，我们可以打出身份牌。\n可不想让马泽奥和瓦利诺斯的关系受影响。

column5: Which is boring, if you ask me.\nI'll try not to say anything witty.\nPirates aren't the best with humor.
column6: 要我说，这挺无聊的。\n我会尽量别说俏皮话。\n海盗可不太懂幽默。

column5: Besides, I'm sure Damek will be there waiting.\nHe'll make sure we get off to the right start.\nWe're going to Mazeo. We'll need protection.
column6: 再说，达梅克肯定会在那儿等着。\n他会确保我们一开始就走对路。\n我们要去马泽奥。我们需要保护。

column5: Maybe Damek will tell us more about that.\nI'm sure there's a lot to catch up on.\nThis Rebellion isn't exactly \"new\".
column6: 也许达梅克能告诉我们更多。\n肯定有很多事要补课。\n这支反抗军可算不上“新”。

column5: I'm willing to bet there's more at play.\nBut with Valinorth, there's nothing secret at all.\nThey're planning to raze our village, plain and simple.
column6: 我敢打赌另有隐情。\n但对付瓦利诺斯，根本没什么秘密可言。\n他们就是打算把我们的村子夷为平地，就这么简单。

column5: You mentioned that it {i}might{/i} be for the blade?\nThat excuse would never fly for an attack this large.\nAt least for Mazeo, they said they were fighting piracy.
column6: 你提过这{i}也许{/i}是为了那把剑？\n这么大的攻势，那种借口根本说不通。\n至少对马泽奥，他们说是为了打击海盗。

column5: I'm sure they want their blade back, but yeah.\nThat desire and this attack are two separate things.\nI'm sure we'll find out the truth if we keep moving forward.
column6: 他们肯定想夺回那把剑，不过也是。\n那个念头和这次袭击是两码事。\n只要继续往前走，我相信我们会查明真相。

column5: That's what worries me about all of this.\nThey push, and we're expected to push back.\nWhat if we don't like fighting...?
column6: 这正是这一切让我担心的地方。\n他们紧逼，我们就得回击。\n可要是我们不喜欢打仗呢……？

column5: That fight-or-die mentality is a terrible thing.\nIt can drive good men to do horrible things.\nPlease, don't let that happen to you, [firstname].
column6: 那种不是你死就是我活的心态太可怕了。\n它能让好人做出可怕的事。\n求你，别让这种事发生在你身上，[firstname]。

column5: That fight-or-die mentality is a terrible thing.\nIt can drive good men to do horrible things.\nPlease, don't let that happen to you, [firstname].
column6: 那种不是你死就是我活的心态太可怕了。\n它能让好人做出可怕的事。\n求你，别让这种事发生在你身上，[firstname]。

column5: Please, don't change too much.\nWe're going to be fighting for peace.\nThat's not worth anything if I can't share it with {i}you{/i}.
column6: 求你，别变太多。\n我们是为和平而战。\n如果不能和你{i}一起{/i}分享，那和平就毫无意义。

column5: Good. I'm glad you're putting thought into it.\nDon't act recklessly in the face of victory.\nVictory is nothing if we can't share it together.
column6: 好。很高兴你在认真思考。\n面对胜利时别鲁莽行事。\n如果不能一起分享，胜利也毫无意义。

column5: I wouldn't mind taking one last look at the village.\nIt's so weird, knowing that an attack is coming.\nThis could be the last time we see our homes?
column6: 我不介意最后再看一眼村子。\n知道袭击将至，感觉真奇怪。\n这可能是我们最后一次见到家园了？

column5: How are we just supposed to accept that?\nI expect we'll have plenty of time to grieve, but...\nIs that something we should really have to do?
column6: 我们怎么能就这么接受？\n我想我们会有很多时间去哀悼，可是……\n这真是我们该承受的吗？

column5: We don't have to look around, but I'd appreciate it.\nIf I find something I want to take with me, I'll grab it.\nI'd much rather leave Valinorth behind with no regrets.
column6: 我们不必四处看看，但我会很感激。\n要是有想带走的东西，我就拿上。\n我更希望能毫无遗憾地离开瓦利诺斯。

column5: Thank you so much, [firstname].\nI can't put my finger on it, but I know I'm not ready.\nOne last walk through Valinorth is all I could ever ask for.
column6: 太谢谢你了，[firstname]。\n我说不清为什么，但我知道自己还没准备好。\n能在瓦利诺斯最后走一走，我就心满意足了。

column5: I understand, but at least try.\nIt's never easy, leaving a life behind. I get that.\nBut one moment now could save you tons of sleepless nights.
column6: 我明白，但至少试着做吧。\n抛下过往的生活从来都不容易，这我懂。\n可现在花一点时间，能替你省去无数个无眠之夜。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: You mean everything that Mylus told us?\nI'm freaking out. I can hardly believe it.\nBut the spirits would never lie to us, right?
column6: 你是说迈勒斯告诉我们的那些？\n我快疯了。我简直不敢相信。\n但灵体绝不会骗我们，对吧？

column5: I can't believe The Triumvirate is our enemy.\nI know they had their reasons with Mazeo, but...\nThere's no reason to attack Valinorth. Not at all!
column6: 我不敢相信三人执政团是我们的敌人。\n我知道他们对马泽奥有他们的理由，可是……\n袭击瓦利诺斯根本毫无理由。完全没有！

column5: Then why don't they ask for it...?\nThere's no need to attack us like this.\nIt makes me wonder if there's more to Mazeo.
column6: 那他们为什么不开口要……？\n没必要这样攻打我们。\n让我不禁怀疑马泽奥的事另有隐情。

column5: They said they took it over to fight piracy.\nBut I think they're acting in their own interest.\nBurning down our village? They don't care about Alestia.
column6: 他们说占领那里是为了打击海盗。\n但我觉得他们是在谋一己之利。\n烧毁我们的村子？他们根本不在乎阿莱斯提亚。

column5: It only makes sense, right?\nIt must have something to do with the spirits.\nTyrants can't stand when something is in their way.
column6: 这不难理解，对吧？\n一定跟灵体有关。\n暴君最受不了有东西挡他们的道。

column5: I'd have a hard time believing that.\nThey don't want the blade. They want us dead.\nStealing is easy. That's not what they're doing here.
column6: 这我可很难相信。\n他们要的不是那把剑。他们要的是我们死。\n偷东西很容易。他们此举可不是偷。

column5: All I can think about is the realm of spirits.\nIt's been getting stronger, but maybe it's too strong?\nMaybe they've started to see it as a threat.
column6: 我满脑子想的都是灵界。\n它一直在变强，但也许强过头了？\n也许他们开始把它视为威胁。

column5: I always thought they were good rulers.\nSometimes you have to make tough decisions.\nMazeo shocked us all, but we've all moved on.
column6: 我一直以为他们是好统治者。\n有时你不得不做出艰难的决定。\n马泽奥的事让我们震惊，但我们都已释怀。

column5: There's also a line you're not meant to cross, though.\nBurning down an innocent village is way past that.\nNo goal could justify what they plan to do with Valinorth.
column6: 但也有不该跨越的底线。\n烧毁一个无辜的村庄，远远越过了那条线。\n他们打算对瓦利诺斯做的事，任何目标都无法为之辩护。

column5: Honestly, I don't know.\nI usually look to you when I think about that.\nBut without spiritual energy? Things will change.
column6: 老实说，我不知道。\n想到这些时，我通常会指望你。\n但没有了灵力？一切都会变。

column5: We're up in mountains, and the spirits keep us warm.\nWithout them, Valinorth would freeze and wilt away.\nWe'd have to migrate to Mazeo, like Mylus said.
column6: 我们身处山中，是灵体让我们保持温暖。\n没有他们，瓦利诺斯会冻僵、凋零。\n我们就得像迈勒斯说的那样，迁往马泽奥。

column5: One thing I know, is that The Triumvirate is ruined.\nThere's no way people will side with this attack.\nIt's only a matter of time before word starts spreading.
column6: 有一点我很确定，三人执政团完了。\n人们不可能支持这次袭击。\n消息传开只是时间问题。

column5: I think I need to concern myself with {i}Alestia's{/i} future.\nThe Rebellion will probably be swarming with new recruits.\nWe can fight back, so no one else loses their home.
column6: 我想我该关心的，是{i}阿莱斯提亚{/i}的未来。\n反抗军大概会涌入大批新兵。\n我们能反击，这样就不会再有别人失去家园。

column5: And it all starts with that special blade.\nI guess we should head to The Grand Tree.\nNo sense leaving without it, right?
column6: 而这一切都始于那把特别的剑。\n我想我们该去巨树了。\n不带它就离开，没道理，对吧？

column5: Sometimes there isn't, you know?\nYou can never change history from your comfort zone.\nIf it's true about you and the blade, I'll have your back.
column6: 你知道，有时候确实没有。\n待在舒适区里，永远改变不了历史。\n如果你和那把剑的传说是真的，我会支持你。

column5: There's something I never thought I'd hear.\nThousands of Seers, and they {i}never{/i} left Valinorth.\nI guess we're meant to play bigger roles than we thought.
column6: 这真是我从没想过会听到的话。\n成千上万的先知，他们{i}从未{/i}离开过瓦利诺斯。\n看来我们注定要扮演比想象中更重要的角色。

column5: But to answer your question? No, I'm not ready.\nUnfortunately, my opinion doesn't count for much.\nI'll have to come to terms with this as we move on.
column6: 但要回答你的问题？不，我还没准备好。\n可惜我的意见没什么分量。\n我只能边走边慢慢接受这一切。

column5: Oh no, I wouldn't want to trouble you.\nYou have enough going on, I'd just be a bother.\nThanks for the offer though, I'll keep it in mind.
column6: 哦，不，我不想麻烦你。\n你已经有够多事要忙，我只会添乱。\n不过谢谢你的好意，我会记在心上。

column5: Really? You seem so calm and collected.\nEither way, it's good to know I'm not alone.\nIf you're ever having trouble, just talk to me.
column6: 真的？你看起来那么沉稳镇定。\n不管怎样，知道我不是一个人就好。\n要是你有难处，随时跟我说。

column5: Really? I guess I'm the odd one out.\nEven Mylus, our Elder, seemed so eager to leave.\nI'd like to see the world, but not under these circumstances.
column6: 真的？看来我是格格不入的那个。\n连我们的长老迈勒斯，看着都那么急着离开。\n我想看看外面的世界，但不是在这样的情形下。

column5: I'll decide when I see it.\nYou and Mylus made it seem really incredible.\nBut at the end of the day, it's just a sword.
column6: 等我见到它再决定吧。\n你和迈勒斯把它说得神乎其神。\n可说到底，它不过是一把剑。

column5: I doubt it'll be the turning point of this battle.\nOf course, I wouldn't mind being proven wrong.\nWhat else can you tell me about it...?
column6: 我怀疑它不会成为这场战斗的转折点。\n当然，我倒不介意被证明是错的。\n你还能告诉我些什么……？

column5: Wait, that's really confusing.\nIt looks like a blade, but serves another purpose?\nTell me more. I'd like to know what makes it special.
column6: 等等，这真让人糊涂。\n它看着像把剑，却有别的用途？\n多说点。我想知道它特别在哪里。

column5: So, it still works as a standard weapon.\nBut I'm curious about the other functions it has.\nWe'd never do this for a run-of-the-mill sword.
column6: 所以，它作为普通武器也照样能用。\n但我对它其他的功能很好奇。\n换成一把普通剑，我们绝不会这么大费周章。

column5: So the more he killed, the more he had to serve him?\nAnd Ulric's life powered a bunch of armored suits...?\nThat means their army could always outnumber Alestia!
column6: 所以杀得越多，就越多人为他效力？\n乌尔里克的性命还驱动了一堆铠甲……？\n那意味着他们的军队永远能压过阿莱斯提亚！

column5: I'm starting to see why it might be a threat.\nBut we won't be stealing life like that, right?\nWe should keep it from them, and limit their numbers.
column6: 我开始明白它为何会是个威胁了。\n但我们不会那样窃取性命，对吧？\n我们该把它从他们手中夺走，限制他们的兵力。

column5: Let's put a pin in that one, alright?\nI don't think we should resort to their means.\nAt that point, what separates the two sides?
column6: 这个先搁一搁，好吗？\n我觉得我们不该效仿他们的手段。\n到了那一步，两方还有什么区别？

column5: We can use it as a weapon, sure.\nBut we shouldn't kill Alestians for greater numbers.\nWe can build a strong army through {i}peaceful{/i} means.
column6: 我们当然可以把它当武器用。\n但不应为了扩充兵力而杀害阿莱斯提亚人。\n我们可以通过{i}和平{/i}的方式组建强大的军队。

column5: Good, I was starting to worry.\nWithout that blade, their army is finite.\nThey can't hide behind numbers like before.
column6: 好，我正开始担心呢。\n没有那把剑，他们的军队是有限的。\n他们没法再像以前那样靠人数取胜。

column5: Come on Gryz, this must be possible.\nEven their Honor Guard barely monitors the place.\nWhen they do, they're oblivious to our existence.
column6: 得了吧，格瑞兹，这一定办得到。\n连他们的荣誉卫队都几乎不监视那里。\n就算监视，他们也察觉不到我们的存在。

column5: If we don't push them, they won't push back.\nAlthough, one final push might be required.\nEither way, we need that deed as a rightful claim.
column6: 我们不去招惹他们，他们就不会反击。\n不过，也许最后还差临门一脚。\n无论如何，我们需要那份地契作为合法的所有权。

column5: Damek, for the last time, it's not so simple!\nIf The Triumvirate knew I was helping you, they'd kill me.\nI wouldn't be surprised if they damaged Mazeo as well.
column6: 达梅克，我最后说一次，没这么简单！\n要是三人执政团知道我帮你，他们会杀了我。\n他们就算毁掉马泽奥，我也不意外。

column5: Oh come on, it's not that risky.\nWe'll operate silently, they'll never know.
column6: 哦，得了吧，没那么多风险。\n我们会悄无声息地行动，他们绝不会知道。

column5: Everything has a paper trail, Damek.\nThey keep track of every step I take.\nAt the end of the day, I'm still their General.
column6: 凡事都会留下书面记录，达梅克。\n我走的每一步他们都盯着。\n说到底，我终究还是他们的将军。

column5: I understand that you want those tunnels.\nBut it would be too risky. They'd find us out.\nI'm not gambling with my life, understand?
column6: 我明白你想要那些隧道。\n但风险太大了。他们会查出我们。\n我不会拿命去赌，明白吗？

column5: With them, it's a gamble, I'll give you that.\nBut with me, I'll have you know it's a certainty.\nI don't think you know how much we need those tunnels.
column6: 跟他们合作，确实是场赌博，这我承认。\n但跟我合作，我让你知道什么叫十拿九稳。\n我看你还不清楚我们有多需要那些隧道。

column5: Damek, is that a threat!?
column6: 达梅克，这是在威胁我吗！？

column5: Of course not, we're too close for that!\nClose enough that you won't have to find out.\nI'm sure we can come to some sort of deal.
column6: 当然不是，我们关系这么近，怎么会！\n近到你根本用不着去猜后果。\n我相信我们能达成某种交易。

column5: Hmph. Mazeo has rubbed off on you.\nI'd expect such tactics from pirates, not you.\nI have to say, you'd need something big to woo me.
column6: 哼。马泽奥把你带坏了。\n这种手段我以为只有海盗才会用，不是你。\n不得不说，你得拿出点大筹码才能打动我。

column5: Damek walks up to the desk, and places some papers down.{w}\nHe looked up at Gryz with a smile, who returned only shock.
column6: 达梅克走到桌前，放下几份文件。{w}\n他微笑着抬头看向格瑞兹，而对方只回以震惊。

column5: They dig for twenty years, and find nothing.\nI use my forces, and we find it in days.\nCorrect me if I'm wrong, but I think this is it?
column6: 他们挖了二十年，一无所获。\n我动用我的部队，几天就找到了。\n要是我说错了请纠正，但我想就是这个吧？

column5: Damek, I don't believe this...\nThis is what I've been looking for.
column6: 达梅克，我简直不敢相信……\n这就是我一直在找的东西。

column5: You must tell me where it is...!
column6: 你必须告诉我在哪儿……！

column5: A deed might sweeten the deal for me.\nBesides, you can report this finding to The Triumvirate.\nThey'll be so ecstatic they won't notice anything else.
column6: 一份地契也许能让这笔交易更合我意。\n再说，你可以把这个发现上报给三人执政团。\n他们会高兴得什么都顾不上。

column5: It is a big deal, and it might sate them.\nBut they'd likely send forces here immediately.\nYou want me to put a target on your new HQ?
column6: 这确实是件大事，也许能让他们满足。\n但他们很可能立刻派兵过来。\n你是要我给你的新总部招来靶子？

column5: Actually, their forces will be preoccupied.\nI have word that they're undertaking another mission.\nWe'll have plenty of time to occupy and fortify.
column6: 其实，他们的兵力会分身乏术。\n我得到消息，他们正在执行另一项任务。\n我们会有充足的时间占领并加固。

column5: I can't believe you've found it, Damek.\nIf you want the deed, you must give me exclusive access.\nNobody else can touch it. I have my plans, and that's final.
column6: 我真不敢相信你找到了，达梅克。\n你想要地契，就得给我独占的权限。\n别人都不许碰。我有我的打算，这事没得商量。

column5: Of course, I'd be more than happy to!\nBut you might have to wait a bit longer.\nTapping into it requires some \"special means\".
column6: 当然，我乐意之至！\n不过你可能要再多等一阵。\n要接通它，需要一些“特殊手段”。

column5: But I promise you won't be waiting much longer.\nSo please, if you would hand over the deed?\nAnd once {i}they{/i} arrive, it's all yours.
column6: 但我保证你不会等太久。\n所以，请把地契交给我吧？\n等{i}他们{/i}一到，一切就归你了。

column5: Sovy left the chambers of his masters, remaining in shock.{w}\nThe truth of things had been explained, and he was surprised.{w}\nHe knew it would take a while before he accepted these revelations.
column6: 索维离开主上的议事厅，仍处在震惊之中。{w}\n事情的真相已被道明，他大为意外。{w}\n他知道，要接受这些真相还得花些时日。

column5: Such a truth, and to think I never knew.\nThis will change everything about my approach.
column6: 竟是这样的真相，我竟一直毫不知情。\n这会彻底改变我的行事方式。

column5: Master? You seem unwell.\nWe leave tomorrow, you should get some rest.\nI know I'm not the one to give orders, but please.
column6: 大人？您看着不太舒服。\n我们明天就出发，您该休息一下。\n我知道轮不到我来下令，但请您务必。

column5: No, it has nothing to do with that.\nIt seems there is more to this attack than we knew.\nThe Triumvirate just finished explaining our true objective.
column6: 不，跟那无关。\n看来这次进攻的内情比我们知道的要多。\n三人执政团刚刚解释了我们真正的目标。

column5: Our \"true\" objective...?\nSovy, what is the meaning of this?
column6: 我们“真正的”目标……？\n索维，这是什么意思？

column5: I don't think I'm able to tell you, Halin.\nThey trusted me alone with this information.\nPerhaps you can visit them on your own time?
column6: 我恐怕不能告诉你，哈林。\n他们只把这件事托付给了我一人。\n也许你可以自己找时间去见他们？

column5: Typical.\nTeasing me with information, and pulling rank.\nI want to prove myself, Sovy. I want to be at your side.
column6: 老样子。\n拿消息吊我胃口，又摆出上级的架子。\n我想证明自己，索维。我想追随在你身边。

column5: Trust me, that would be wonderful.\nBut this is different. It changes everything.\nIt would better to hear it directly from them.
column6: 相信我，那会很好。\n但这次不一样。这件事改变一切。\n最好还是直接听他们说。

column5: Alright, alright.\nI have to say, you seem quite distressed.\nI'll go talk to them, but take my advice and rest.
column6: 好吧，好吧。\n不得不说，你看着很不安。\n我去见他们，但听我一句，去休息吧。

column5: I'm afraid there's no time for that, Halin.\nI'm going to speak with the prisoner. He's coming, too.
column6: 恐怕没时间了，哈林。\n我要去跟那个囚犯谈谈。他也要一起去。

column5: Shane is coming with us...?\nSovy, that doesn't make any sense.
column6: 肖恩要跟我们一起……？\n索维，这说不通。

column5: It seems a run-in with the Rebels is likely.\nTo that end, I've come up with a fitting punishment.\nWhen you're done with our Masters, meet me back here.
column6: 看来很可能会跟反抗军遭遇。\n为此，我想出了一个恰当的惩罚。\n你见完主上之后，回这儿找我。

column5: Yes, of course.\nI'm ready to take action at a moment's notice.\nAnd now, something tells me, we will be.
column6: 好的，当然。\n我随时准备立刻行动。\n而现在，我有预感，我们很快就会行动。

column5: We can sail to Mazeo in under a day.\nThere's a ship waiting for us at the Balteus docks.\nAs soon as Halin arrives, we'll be free to go.
column6: 我们不到一天就能航行到马泽奥。\n有艘船在巴尔泰乌斯的码头等着我们。\n哈林一到，我们就能出发。

column5: Odd choice of words. I highly doubt I'll be free to go.\nThough I'm a little excited that Halin is coming along.\nHe was much better than you. More threatening, as well.
column6: 用词真奇怪。我可不太相信我会有“自由”可言。\n不过哈林也一起去，我还挺高兴的。\n他比你强多了。也更有威慑力。

column5: Shane, this isn't about being threatening.\nIt's about who can put their foot down when they need to.\nHalin is all talk. Lots of promises, but no follow-through.
column6: 肖恩，重点不在威不威慑。\n而在于谁能在该强硬时强硬。\n哈林只会嘴上说说。承诺一堆，从不兑现。

column5: Right, of course. Thanks for the heads up.\nI'll remember that next time he tries interrogating me.\nIf I didn't know any better, I'd say you didn't like him.
column6: 对，当然。多谢提醒。\n下次他审我时我会记住这点。\n要不是我了解你，我会说你不太喜欢他。

column5: I doubt he's long for this world.\nA Grand Inquisitor needs to be more than talk.\nThat, and I work {i}much{/i} better when I'm alone.
column6: 我看他活不长。\n大审判官可不能只会耍嘴皮子。\n再说，我{i}独自{/i}办事效率高得多。

column5: Working alone, huh?\nI don't think that's a very good idea.\nWhat if you get into a bind? Who'd help you then?
column6: 独自办事，是吧？\n我觉得这不是什么好主意。\n要是你陷入困境呢？那时谁来帮你？

column5: I don't get into binds, Shane.\nI'm more in the habit of putting them on others.
column6: 我不会陷入困境，肖恩。\n我更习惯让别人陷入困境。

column5: Yeah, we'll see how far that gets you.\nSo what's the plan, anyway? Attacking Valinorth?\nYou want the blade back. Halin made it pretty clear.
column6: 是啊，那就看看这能让你走多远。\n那到底有什么计划？攻打瓦利诺斯？\n你们想把剑夺回去。哈林说得很明白。

column5: Now why would I tell you that...?\nDon't assume camaraderie between us.
column6: 我为什么要告诉你……？\n别以为我们之间有什么情谊。

column5: Fine, fine. Just trying to get involved.
column6: 行行行。我只是想参与进来罢了。

column5: So you can write your Rebel friends, no doubt.\nDon't try anything, Shane. I'm watching you.
column6: 好给你那帮反抗军朋友写信，毫无疑问。\n别耍花样，肖恩。我盯着你呢。

column5: Besides, Valinorth is an insignificant part of our plan.\nWhen we're finished, Alestia will be forever changed.
column6: 再说，瓦利诺斯在我们的计划里无足轻重。\n等我们大功告成，阿莱斯提亚将永远改变。

column5: The tunnels underneath Mazeo were quiet, almost eerily so.{w}\nGryz and Damek met in secret, not deep enough to run into trouble.{w}\nAny further though, and they'd cross paths with The Triumvirate's Honor Guard.
column6: 马泽奥地下的隧道寂静无声，静得近乎诡异。{w}\n格瑞兹和达梅克秘密会面，所在之处还不算深，不至于惹上麻烦。{w}\n可再往里走，就会撞上三人执政团的荣誉卫队。

column5: I guess that settles it. The deed is yours.\nYou have lots of work to do, Damek. What comes first?
column6: 看来就这么定了。地契归你了。\n你有很多活要干，达梅克。先做什么？

column5: Lots of dusting, I presume.\nThough there's something odd about these tunnels.\nThe Honor Guard has no need to eat, sleep, or socialize.
column6: 先打扫灰尘吧，我猜。\n不过这些隧道有点古怪。\n荣誉卫队不需要吃饭、睡觉，也不需要交际。

column5: Being empty suits of armor, they need none of that.\nBut go any deeper, and you'll see an entire hideout.\nBedrooms, training rooms, a library, and more.
column6: 他们是空荡荡的铠甲，自然什么都不需要。\n可再往深处走，你会看到一整个藏身之所。\n卧室、训练室、图书馆，还有更多。

column5: Maybe that's why they never found what we were after.\nThey were too busy building some sort of utopia.
column6: 也许这就是他们一直没找到我们要找的东西的原因。\n他们忙着建造某种乌托邦去了。

column5: It'll be easy to fortify against attacks.\nThey've practically done it for us, already.\nI just wish I knew why. It's so peculiar.
column6: 要设防抵御进攻会很容易。\n他们几乎都替我们做好了。\n我只希望能知道为什么。太奇怪了。

column5: I have a theory of my own, actually.
column6: 其实，我有个自己的猜想。

column5: And what is that?
column6: 是什么？

column5: You know how those things are created, yes?\nThe Grand Inquisitor, and that life-stealing sword.\nWell, he was at my side when we occupied Mazeo.
column6: 你知道那些东西是怎么造出来的，对吧？\n大审判官，还有那把窃取性命之剑。\n当年我们占领马泽奥时，他就在我身边。

column5: I see...
column6: 我明白了……

column5: The members of the Honor Guard that wander these tunnels.\nI think they're the spirits of those we killed, Damek.\nPerhaps they just want to continue living. It's heartbreaking.
column6: 在这些隧道里游荡的荣誉卫队成员。\n我觉得他们是被我们杀死之人的灵，达梅克。\n也许他们只是想继续活着。真令人心碎。

column5: That's an understatement...\nBut it explains the beds, and living quarters.\nAnd if they retain some memory, they'd hate The Triumvirate.
column6: 这说得太轻了……\n但这解释了那些床铺和起居空间。\n要是他们还留有记忆，一定会恨三人执政团。

column5: Yeah, which is why they never completed their job.\nOr at the very least, intentionally threw their progress.
column6: 是啊，所以他们从没完成过任务。\n至少也是故意拖慢进度。

column5: A theory with merit, I'll give you that much.\nBut now that we've found what you're after, what happens?\nI think you should tell me what you really want with it.
column6: 这猜想有价值，这点我认可。\n可既然我们已经找到了你要的东西，接下来呢？\n我觉得你该告诉我，你到底想拿它做什么。

column5: You can think all you want, but it won't happen.\nJust know that I'm looking to make up for something.\nI can never undo the occupation, but I have an idea...
column6: 你尽管猜，但我不会说。\n你只要知道，我是想弥补些什么。\n我永远无法抹去那场占领，但我有个主意……

column5: Very well, whenever you're ready.
column6: 好吧，随你什么时候说。

column5: As long as I have the deed, I'm satisfied.\nWhen [firstname] arrives, however, I'd love to hear more.
column6: 只要地契在手，我就满足了。\n不过等[firstname]到了，我倒很想多听听。

column5: As long as I have the deed, I'm satisfied.\nWhen [firstname] arrives, however, I'd love to hear more.
column6: 只要地契在手，我就满足了。\n不过等[firstname]到了，我倒很想多听听。
